clock: UTC Unix seconds; prediction timestamp is acquisition T; state and features use observations at or before T.
future_window: An onset qualifies only when T < onset <= T + horizon. An already-active target is detection, not forecasting.
exclusions: At evaluation only: gaps beyond the target coverage bound, insufficient future coverage, right-censored windows, and unobservable latent onsets are uncertain, not healthy. Charge uncertain interruptions to the nuisance budget conservatively.
qualification: At least 10 observable holdout events and 40% useful-lead recall and 50% episode precision; safety, parity, p95 <100 ms, <=0.5 false or uncertain interruptions/day, <=5% backup/build nuisance. Require development and validation qualification for a GO.

cpu.event: Sustained contextual workload pressure, not CPU hardware failure
cpu.context: RAM >=85% or selected nonresponding process count >=2
cpu.onset: First independent usable sample confirming 300 seconds of contextual high CPU and six independent observations
cpu.observability: An independent causal detector must confirm the target while the latent event remains active.

disk_capacity.event: Selected volume crossing a 10% free capacity boundary; not drive failure
disk_capacity.context: One fixed selected volume per offline run
disk_capacity.onset: First usable distinct reading at or below 10% free; latent truth is evaluated at 15 s resolution
disk_capacity.observability: A fresh crossing must be observed between the latent onset and recovery; cached readings are not independent confirmations.

process.event: Sustained selected-process responsiveness degradation; not crash or hardware failure
process.context: CPU workload may qualify supporting evidence; process identity is subsystem-scoped because per-process IDs are unavailable
process.onset: First independent usable sample confirming 360 seconds and at least six observations with selected nonresponse count >=3
process.observability: A causal detector must confirm sustained degradation before latent recovery.
